key_insight: Rear-jet blockage encloses a recirculation region that enhances momentum exchange through larger mixing scales, diluting the front jet while the shielded rear jet rises higher.
engineering_relevance: Tandem-jet designs should account for gap-driven momentum loss and unequal penetration rather than treating each jet as an isolated jet in crossflow.
method: 40 kHz time-resolved PIV across nine spacing–velocity-ratio conditions.
DMD and SPOD to assess unsteady shear-layer dynamics.
evidence_signal: Across 68 twin-jet cases and 11 single-jet records, front-jet near-field length decreased by up to 40%, while gap exchange exceeded the single-jet leeward reference by up to 1.5× in zone peak and 2.8× when area-integrated.
watch_item: The mechanism is supported observationally; the absence of growing modes applies only within the resolved frequency band and record length.
paper_title: Tandem jets in crossflow: the enclosed-recirculation momentum exchange and the unsteady shear-layer dynamics
